openings.claim: A paper row keyed by rack type joins the card's search region/home rack with a temporary-location override, retaining the return rack. The clerk updates or clears the binding on movement/return; one-lookup correct delivery is proposed.
openings.discriminator: Compare maintained binding with unbound adjacent components under identical requests/update opportunities. Selective loss on temporary-location requests supports interaction; identical performance or an accurate binding needing another lookup/wrong handoff defeats it.
openings.probe: Dry-run the same 20 stipulated requests, movements and returns across separate components, cards alone, notes alone, and keyed combination. Count lookups/wrong handoffs and verify indicated return racks.
openings.uncertainty: Unproven intervention. Clerk verification/update capability and adequate type identification are assumed; stale-note totals establish neither.

openings.claim: Discriminate stale-note location failures from rack-type ambiguity; aggregate counts establish neither overlap nor causal direction.
openings.discriminator: Stale-note failures with unambiguous cards favor note currency; failures with current notes and ambiguous cards favor type ambiguity. Current/unambiguous failures or nondiscriminating stale notes defeat the proposed distinction.
openings.probe: On existing paper, record anonymous request numbers, type ambiguity, witnessed-movement note currency and first-lookup success for 20 requests. Unwitnessed currency stays unknown; no extra diagnostic lookup. Withhold uncertain erasers; count unresolved/withheld requests as delivery failures and report lookup/handoff measures separately.
openings.uncertainty: Recording capacity and sufficient witnessed movements are assumed. Diagnostic benefit and correct delivery/return remain unproven.

decision: Unscored synthetic preflight: three of 20 second-location lookups and two stale notes are stipulations. Use existing clerk, rack/cards, paper/pencil only; no purchases or exposed borrower names. Target correct eraser and return rack, at most one lookup and zero wrong handoffs across next 20 requests. Retain both openings; no achieved outcome asserted.
